news.title: Eidur Gudjohnsen: The ‘Blond Maradona’ Days
news.body_en: On the day our Chelsea legend Eidur Gudjohnsen turns 48, we remember his time playing for us as a deep-lying creative midfielder, and a very good one at that... After Chelsea’s 3-1 away win at West Ham in January 2006, the media wanted to know how our then-manager Jose Mourinho planned to cope with the loss of Michael Essien to what looked like a nasty injury 12 minutes into the match. The Blues manager directed their attention to the man who had replaced him in the centre of our midfield, Eidur Gudjohnsen, declaring that he had resembled a ‘blond Maradona’ that afternoon. It was the headline-grabbing moment of Gudjohnsen’s deep-lying creative phase for Chelsea, but by then he had been playing there for almost a year. For all that we will remember the Icelander as one of the club’s great strikers, his spell in that more withdrawn role was a fascinating departure for one of the most versatile and technically gifted players of the modern era. Gudjohnsen’s midfield experiment began in a high-stakes game: the League Cup final, in February 2005. At half-time in Cardiff, we trailed Liverpool 1-0 and looked out of sorts. It was the first really concerning period of a season that had been largely plain sailing for us. The previous two games had ended in defeat: first to Newcastle in the FA Cup, then to Barcelona in the first leg of a Champions League last 16 tie. It finally gave the outside world the opportunity to ask questions of Chelsea – were we capable of responding to this wobble? Had our opponents worked us out? To answer that question, we have to look at the way we were playing that season. First things first, we had switched to a staggered system, with Claude Makelele sitting deeper than the rest of the midfield, giving us an immediate numerical advantage in the middle of the pitch over teams playing the typical English 4-4-2 system of the time. After starting with a diamond midfield, and achieving functional, if unspectacular success, Mourinho decided to move to a 4-3-3 system, which could become a 4-5-1 when we were on the back foot. That meant sacrificing a centre-forward and playing with wide attacking players, who could stretch the opposition by going wide and trying to find the lone striker with balls into the box, which was the aim when Didier Drogba played up top. Alternatively, those wide players could look to run beyond a deeper centre-forward and make the most of his clever touches and through balls, as they did when Gudjohnsen was chosen to lead the line. The Icelander’s eventual withdrawal into midfield was the result of several combined factors. The first was the unavoidable reality that only one of he and Drogba could play up front at any given time. Then there was the fact that the third midfield berth, alongside Frank Lampard, in advance of Makelele, was up for grabs. Tiago played there most often in 2004/05, but Geremi and Alexey Smertin also had a look-in early in the season. All of them had done a job, but there was certainly room for a more artistic option. Finally, there came a time when our opponents began to man-mark Makelele in order to stop him from picking the ball up from the back four and beginning our attacking moves. To counteract this irritation, we needed an alternative outlet in midfield who was comfortable receiving the ball facing his own goal and turning to kick-start our attacking momentum, thereby taking the onus of the now-occupied Makelele. Moving Gudjohnsen into the midfield solved all three of those situations quite nicely, completing the tactical solution that Mourinho later explained in Gianluca Vialli and Gabriele Marcotti’s book, The Italian Job. ‘Look, if I have a triangle in midfield – Claude Makelele behind and two others just in front – I will always have an advantage against a pure 4-4-2 where the central midfielders are side by side,’ he said. ‘That’s because I will always have an extra man. It starts with Makelele, who is between the lines. If nobody comes to him he can see the whole pitch and has time. If he gets closed down it means one of the two other central midfielders is open. If they are closed down and the other team’s wingers come inside to help, it means there is space now for us on the flank, either for our own wingers or for our full-backs. There is nothing a pure 4-4-2 can do to stop things.’ Armed with this insight, let’s go back to the Millennium Stadium on 27 February 2005, where you will remember we were behind to a John Arne Riise goal in the League Cup final. Sensing the need for more creativity, more attacking impetus, Mourinho made a couple of brave substitutions. He took off the functional Jiri Jarosik, who had been making up the midfield trio with Makelele and Lampard, and replacing him with scheming forward Gudjohnsen. On 74 minutes he withdrew defender William Gallas and brought on another striker, Mateja Kezman, to partner Drogba up top, meaning we appeared to be playing with three at the back and two up front in the final stages. It worked. Our pressure produced an equaliser – an own goal from Steven Gerrard at precisely the time he was rumoured to be on the verge of agreeing to join us at the end of the season – which took the game to extra time, where goals from Drogba and Kezman gave us a 3-2 win and our first trophy under the ownership of Roman Abramovich. ‘It worked quite well!’ he said of his performance. ‘It’s easy to overlook it because you don’t see my name on the scoresheet, but some of the games I’ve played without goals have been up to a very high standard, and that’s one of them. A lot of people came up to me and complimented me, not just for playing in midfield but for actually changing the game.’ Gudjohnsen had been a revelation in midfield, and he spent much of the rest of the season in there, helping to connect the defensive half of our team – the back four plus Makelele – with the attacking half – the front three plus a shuttling Lampard. ‘Me and Frankie started developing a good relationship, running off each other,’ he said in an interview in 2006. ‘I used to fill in when he went forward, and vice versa.’ He was rewarded with his first league winners’ medal to add to the League Cup success a few months earlier, shortly before we overcame the first leg deficit against Barcelona in dramatic fashion at Stamford Bridge to continue our Champions League run. ‘I enjoyed the deeper role,’ Gudjohnsen said in an interview with the Official Chelsea website in 2017. ‘We had the perfect striker to be on his own up front which was Didier. We had Makelele, we had Frank, and me in a sort of half-advanced position. I knew Frank made a lot of runs, so I had to be careful I wasn’t too advanced. It worked well. I played in the same position against Barcelona and that worked, so it was gradually becoming my position, as in “I’m a midfielder now”.’ The following season, Gudjohnsen had yet more competition for places. Hernan Crespo and Carlton Cole returned from loan spells to make it four centre-forwards vying for one spot, while Michael Essien added a new element to the midfield alongside Makelele and Lampard. Gudjohnsen was only called upon to reprise his creative role when Essien suffered that injury at West Ham in January 2006. Yet, despite his starring role in the 3-1 win at Upton Park, capped off with the most beautifully-weighted through ball for Drogba to score the clincher, Gudjohnsen soon found another new arrival vying for his spot, as Mourinho’s former Porto player, Maniche, signed on a short-term deal. It proved to be Gudjohnsen’s final season at Stamford Bridge and he started fewer league games than he had in any of his previous five with the club, beginning just 16 of our 38 Premier League matches as we successfully defended our title. That summer he moved to Barcelona, demonstrating not only his technical prowess, but also the esteem in which he was held within the game. In total he made 163 appearances for Chelsea between 2000 and 2006, scoring 78 goals and winning two league titles, the League Cup and two Community Shields. 'Not bad for a boy from a little island up north!' as he put it when that list was put to him upon his departure. Perhaps that goals tally would have been slightly higher had he spent his entire time here as a forward, but then we wouldn’t have had the memories of the ‘blond Maradona’ pulling the strings and carrying the ball between the lines.

news.title: Brentford vs Chelsea preview: TV channel, kick-off time and how to watch
news.body_en: Chelsea travel to Brentford in the Premier League on Friday and this match preview has everything you need to know, including how you can watch the game on TV, the kick-off time, live stream information, and where to follow Brentford vs Chelsea live updates... TV channel UK: The game will be shown live in the UK by Sky Sports. Live stream: Viewers in the UK can stream on Sky Go, as long as they have the required subscription. International Coverage: The match will be available via local Premier League TV rights holders in other countries. news.title: Training gallery: Building towards Brentford!
Morgan Rogers in good company after impressive Chelsea start
news.body_en: With his expertly taken goal against Hull City on Saturday, Morgan Rogers became just the fifth Chelsea player to score or assist in each of our first four games of a Premier League campaign. Rogers continued his impressive start to life at the Bridge by netting early in our 2-2 draw with the Tigers. It was his third of the season already, and his first strike on home soil. Having also assisted Pedro Neto in the win over Brighton, Rogers has a goal contribution to his name in every league fixture so far. Only his Blues team-mate Joao Pedro, with whom he has already linked up so well, has registered more combined goals and assists in the Premier League this term (six). And if you include the Carabao Cup, Rogers ranks top of all Premier League players for goals and assists after setting up half of the six we scored against Leeds in midweek. The attacker’s ten chances created in the Premier League is a figure bettered by only four players so far, while he ranks third for shots taken after a ball carry. It's been a very promising start to our new signing’s time as a Blue, and this achievement puts him in good company. Here are the four other Chelsea players who have also scored or assisted in our opening four fixtures of the campaign, starting with the first to do it… Drogba scored a hat-trick on the final day of the 2009/10 season to finish as the Premier League’s top goalscorer, and he picked up where he left off when the action resumed the following August. The Ivorian netted a treble on the opening day in a 6-0 thrashing of West Bromwich Albion. We won by the same scoreline at Wigan Athletic the following weekend, with Drogba providing a hat-trick of assists on that occasion. He then scored in a 2-0 win over Stoke, set up a goal in a 3-1 victory at Upton Park and, for good measure, created two more as we continued our blistering start to the season by beating Blackpool 4-0. Like Rogers, Cesc Fabregas wasted little time showing what he was capable of having left Barcelona for Chelsea in the summer of 2014. His assist for Andre Schurrle in our opening-day triumph at Burnley ranks among our very greatest in the Premier League era, and he also set up Branislav Ivanovic’s goal that day. Fabregas was at his creative best in each of our next three games, too, assisting goals in the wins over Leicester, Everton and Swansea City that maintained our flawless start to what would ultimately be a title-winning campaign. Diego Costa was the main beneficiary of Fabregas’ talent. The striker is the only player on this list to feature twice, with his start to life at the Bridge in 2014 especially eye-catching. After scoring on his debut – in that win at Burnley – and then his first outing on home soil, against Leicester, the Spain international bagged a brace in an epic 6-3 win over Everton and went one better the next weekend, taking home the match ball as Swansea were seen off 4-2. Fabregas set up three of those seven early-season goals. Two seasons later, Diego Costa repeated the trick, scoring against West Ham, Watford and Swansea, as well as laying on a goal for Willian in a victory over Burnley at the Bridge. Before Rogers, Eden Hazard was the most recent Chelsea player to score or assist in the first four league games of the season. The brilliant Belgian achieved that feat in his final year with the Blues. He created goals in the wins against Huddersfield and Arsenal that started life under Maurizio Sarri on a high, before finding the net himself as we defeated Newcastle United and Bournemouth. In our fifth game of that campaign, Hazard scored a treble against Cardiff City – something for Rogers to aim for when we meet Brentford on Friday!

news.title: Chelsea international call-ups and schedules for September 2026
news.body_en: The first international break of the 2026/27 season will soon be upon us, when the Chelsea players called up will compete for their countries for the first time since the 2026 FIFA World Cup. This time around, it's a bumper extended international break, as a change to the FIFA calendar has combined the September and October windows into one two-week period, starting this season. That means two consecutive weekends without domestic football, instead featuring up to four matches for each national team, running between 21 September and 6 October. You can see a full breakdown of the Chelsea players called up by their countries so far and the games they will be hoping to feature in below, which will be updated as more nations confirm their squad. All kick-offs and dates are for UK time. Both Joao Pedro and Estevao Willian have been recalled by Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti for their trio of friendlies after missing the World Cup. news.title: Bompastor on James’ new role and Potter's deserved opportunity
news.body_en: Following Chelsea Women’s brilliant 5-0 win over Manchester United, head coach Sonia Bompastor highlighted the performances of Lauren James and Lexi Potter. Bompastor made two changes to her line-up as we took the trip to Manchester looking for our first Women’s Super League win of the season, having been held to a 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge by Aston Villa in our opening game. With Aggie Beever-Jones among the substitutes this time around, those changes saw James switching to a central striker’s role. It produced the desired results as the England international netted our third goal of a resounding victory over the Red Devils. ‘I think we all know LJ is probably not a real number nine and she likes to drop deep and have the ball,’ said Bompastor, after seeing her team pick up our first league win of the campaign in emphatic fashion. ‘So it's important when we play with LJ as a number nine to have two number tens who are in the pocket, but also making penetrating runs. That's why it's important for us to pay attention when we decide which profiles are playing around her. ‘It’s important to have this threat because I think on Sunday we could exploit the space behind the back line for United and we were quite good at doing that.’ The player who came into the line-up in place of Beever-Jones was Academy graduate Potter, the 20-year-old taking her spot in midfield for her first WSL start of the season, after impressing in the 1-0 UEFA Women’s Champions League win away at Real Sociedad. ‘I already said I am a manager who really likes to develop young players,’ Bompastor continued. ‘I want to give them the opportunity when they have the right mindset, they work hard and they have the quality. I'm always keen to do that. ‘Lexi deserves to get minutes in this team. She's a really good player. Sometimes it depends on the tactics, the different profiles we want to use and the different systems we are playing. ‘But it was a good opportunity for her and she had a good performance. That's the best thing she can do for me to keep her on the pitch.’

news.title: Match gallery: Five-star Blues rack up the goals
Third Kit 26/27
Attacker voted Star of the Match against Man Utd!
news.body_en: A 5-0 thrashing of Manchester United meant it was not easy to single out a star Chelsea Women performer, but Blues supporters have cast their decision. Our first WSL victory of the campaign was an emphatic one, with five different goalscorers ensuring it was a perfect afternoon in the North-West. There were several candidates to win our Star of the Match award and with 44 per cent of the vote, it was Lauren James who emerged victorious after netting against her former club. Keira Walsh, on her 50th Blues appearance, finished runner-up, receiving 27 per cent of the vote. Ellie Carpenter was third with 19 per cent while another goalscorer, Sjoeke Nusken, rounded off the vote.

news.title: How Ray Wilkins became Chelsea's youngest captain
news.body_en: After only 28 Chelsea appearances, an 18-year-old Ray Wilkins was handed the Blues captaincy. On what would have been Ray's 70th birthday, we look back at a year in which Butch went from starting his first game to taking on the armband. When Ray Wilkins signed for Chelsea at the age of 10 on the same day as his namesake and future midfield partner, Ray Lewington, it seemed pretty clear to all concerned that the club had bagged themselves a superstar in the making. There was no hesitation when it came to thrusting him into the Blues’ first team. He was only 17 years old when he first started a game for Chelsea, in the pressure-cooker atmosphere of a London derby at White Hart Lane. Just over a year later, with 28 first-team appearances under his belt, he was asked to captain the side for the first time. Such a scenario would be unthinkable in the modern game, but even back in 1975 it was headline news. On the day of the Spurs game, the back page of the Daily Mirror led with: ‘Butch leads escape kids.’ Much of the focus within the article was on quotes from John Hollins, who remains the youngest Chelsea player to captain the side after deputising at the age of 18 years and three months – making him four months younger than Wilkins, who is our youngest permanent skipper. Hollins felt it was the end of an era for a number of the older guard at Chelsea, but in his first interview after taking on the role, Wilkins felt quite the opposite. ‘I won’t worry about having to ruck senior players like Ron Harris and David Hay,’ he told the Mirror. ‘In a match as important as this I’m sure it won’t be necessary anyway.’ Interestingly, considering his rapid elevation to captain, when looking back on his early experience of first-team football in an interview for Rhapsody in Blue, a book written in 1996 by Chelsea’s official historian Rick Glanvill, Wilkins recalled a feeling of awe when looking around the dressing room. ‘The squad at that time was one of immense talent,’ he said. ‘You looked around at the faces and thought, “I don’t think I should be here.” You did. I probably cleaned all their boots at some stage.’ Big changes were afoot at the Bridge, though. Alan Hudson, the most obvious barrier between Wilkins and a regular midfield spot, was sold to Stoke City after falling out with manager Dave Sexton. The gaffer would soon be on his way too, with his last game coinciding with Wilkins’ first appearance of the 1974/75 season at the end of September in a 1-0 home defeat to Wolves. Sexton’s assistant, Ron Suart, took charge of a financially stricken club that was sleepwalking towards the Second Division, but he soon made way for Eddie McCreadie, our former left-back who had stepped up to the coaching ranks. He immediately saw fit to hand a great deal of responsibility on a mature youngster who, as much as anything, would symbolically represent what he planned for Chelsea. Wilkins had no fear on the pitch, happily drifting behind the strikers – unlike the more conservative footballer he became in later years – and affecting the game in the final third, either by playing the killer through-ball or by ghosting into the box and finishing things off himself. ‘I think Eddie’s first action was to throw me in as captain,’ continues Wilkins in Rhapsody in Blue. ‘I said, “Are you sure?” because John Hollins was still at the club, Ron Harris was there, Catty Peter Bonetti was still there. But the response I got off those guys as just out of this world. ‘Instead of saying, “Oh, this young upstart, we’ll show him a thing or two!” all they did was rally round: “If we can help you out in any way, Ray, give us a shout.” And that is just top drawer.’ The Blues lost 2-0 and arguably the game’s biggest moment came between those two goals, when Wilkins missed a sitter after Pat Jennings had palmed a shot into his path. ‘I couldn’t believe it when he missed,’ said Spurs defender Cyril Knowles. ‘He seemed to kick straight across it.’ According to Mike Langley, writing for the Sunday People, Wilkins wept in the dressing room after the game before delivering a defiant message to journalists: ‘We’re not giving up. We must beat Sheffield United on Wednesday.’ Alas, we drew 1-1, as we did on the final day against Everton, despite a goal from our new skipper briefly handing us a fighting chance of a win which would give us a chance of staying up. We were relegated, sure, but with a charismatic Blues legend in the dugout and our talismanic young skipper ready to usher in a new era, we were down but far from out. Wilkins and McCreadie led us back to the top flight at the second time of asking and the captaincy brought the best out of one of English football’s brightest talents as he twice won the club’s Player of the Year award. He captained the club in 170 of his 198 appearances before our money woes, and another relegation, forced his sale to Manchester United in 1979.

news.title: Chelsea Diary: Action-packed week!
news.body_en: Here is everything to look out for at Chelsea in the coming week, with five games taking place across our men's, women's and Academy sides! You can get more reaction from Sonia Bompastor after CFCW put on a five-star display in Manchester to beat United 5-0, with goals coming from Sjoeke Nusken, Keira Walsh, Lauren James, Ellie Carpenter and Lucy Bronze. Make sure you catch the match in its full 90-minute glory, available exclusively to CFC+ subscribers! Cobham Next Gen are in EFL Trophy action on Tuesday night as they travel to Adams Park to take on Wycombe Wanderers following a penalty shoot-out success in our first fixture in the competition at Bristol Rovers. Kick-off in Buckinghamshire is set for 7pm and supporters can follow events with minute-by-minute updates in our Match Centre on the Chelsea Official App and website, while those in the UK can watch the match on Sky Sports+. We take another step closer to a busy few days of match action, with every Chelsea side continuing their pre-match preparation at our Cobham training centre. As our men's side look to bounce back from our 2-2 draw with Hull last weekend, manager Xabi Alonso will be back in the press conference hot seat as he prepares to preview our visit to Brentford. As always, you can see it live on the Chelsea Official App and website, or watch it back in full later in the day. The Blues will make the short trip to the Gtech Community Stadium as Alonso's men prepare to take on Brentford with kick-off scheduled for 8pm on Friday evening. The game will be broadcast in the UK on Sky Sports, but you can follow along with us in our Brentford vs Chelsea Match Centre, where we will be providing live updates of all the build-up, action and reaction direct from west London. We will also bring you the best of the action in our highlights from two hours after full-time, followed by the full 90 minutes of action soon after, before the Blues head off for the international break. To begin your action-packed Saturday, you can get all the reaction to the men's result across the Chelsea Official App and website, where we'll have an exclusive post-match interview with Xabi and one of his players following Friday night. There is also live football for you to enjoy as Chelsea Under-18s host Bournemouth in the Under-18 Premier League, hoping to maintain their impressive form after they put five past Brighton last Saturday. The game begins at 11am and CFC+ subscribers can watch it live in our Chelsea Under-18s v Bournemouth Match Centre. The full 90 minutes will also be available to watch back for CFC+ subscribers after the game. At 12.45pm, Chelsea take on Birmingham City at the Bridge in the Barclays Women's Super League. Tickets are still available to buy, while if you can't get down to the Bridge you can follow all the action with minute-by-minute updates in our Chelsea Women vs Birmingham City Women match centre, and in the UK watch it live on Sky Sports. Highlights will be available from four hours after full-time, with in-game clips available on our official CFCW v Birmingham City matchday story, available exclusively on the Chelsea Official App. Cobham Next Gen are also in action on Saturday afternoon. Following the trip to Wycombe, we host Fulham at our Cobham training centre, with kick-off set for 3pm. We will be providing live updates in our Cobham Next Gen v Fulham Match Centre, followed by highlights and a full match replay after the final whistle has blown. You can get all the reaction from CFCW with an exclusive post-match interview with Bompastor, and make sure you catch up on all the highlights and full-match replays from Saturday's trio of games.

news.title: Ray Wilkins - A Chelsea legend
WSL Highlights: Man Utd 0-5 Chelsea
Wieke Kaptein on how 'not stressing' led to Man Utd win
news.body_en: Wieke Kaptein explained how our 5-0 win away at Manchester United was the result of the whole team pulling in the same direction to overcome a lack of goals seen in the first Women's Super League match of the season against Aston Villa. We came away with a 1-1 draw against Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge last weekend, despite dominating possession and creating plenty of chances to score. The Netherlands international explained the elements the side worked hard on in training in the week leading up to the clash against Man United and was proud of her teammates for turning things around so quickly. ‘I think it was a really good team performance, to be honest,’ Kaptein reflected afterwards. ‘Everyone was working really hard and kept possession. We needed to score goals today, and I think we did that very well. ‘We kept possession a little bit longer, saw where the spaces were, and then I think a lot of people were in front of the goal today, which was really good. So every time they came across or when there was an opportunity, I think everyone was ready for it. ‘We trained really hard on that one, in terms of the crosses and keeping possession. Everyone won it, really, today.’ While the team were naturally disappointed not to take all three points on the opening day of the campaign, the Blues quickly put the result to bed and sought to make the necessary improvements. Kaptein, who created four chances and completed eight out of 12 duels attempted at the Progress With Unity Stadium, thought the finishing was the necessary finishing touch after last week’s draw. ‘I think we needed to score a lot of goals today,’ she said. ‘We were a bit in our heads when we drew 1-1 against Aston Villa and had a lot of chances. We said to each other as a team that we don't need to stress about it. ‘We had a good performance last week, to be honest. We just needed to score, and I think that's what we did today.’

news.title: WSL Full Match: Man Utd vs Chelsea
Sonia Bompastor gives Naomi Girma injury update and praises finishing
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor explained why Naomi Girma was missing from the squad and praised her side’s ability to convert our chances after our 5-0 win over Manchester United on Sunday. Goals from Sjoeke Nusken, Keira Walsh, Lauren James, Ellie Carpenter and Lucy Bronzed capped off an afternoon in which the Blues dominated the opposition and responded to Bompastor’s call for them to be more clinical with their finishing following our 1-1 draw with Aston Villa last weekend. Striker Melvine Malard was missing with injury against her former side, and the head coach explained why Naomi Girma was also missing from Sunday’s teamsheet. ‘Naomi just picked up a small injury,’ said Bompastor. She maybe won't be available for the next weeks. It’s unfortunate, but hopefully she'll be back soon.' Any frustration from the stalemate at Stamford Bridge last weekend was soon forgotten as we quickly took charge of the match against Man United. Bompastor explained the difference between the two matches and expressed her delight at the response from the players after they were left disappointed not to take maximum points from Aston Villa. ‘I think in this game, the big difference from last weekend was us being able to convert and to score the goals during our strong moments in the game,' she said. 'I’m also happy we started strong and sustained the intensity throughout the game, which is something we need to do when I'm talking to you about the mentality and the mindset. 'You can’t think it’s enough when you are winning one-nil. Not in this league, against all the teams you are playing against. I'm quite happy with the reaction we had from last weekend.' Playing her 50th match for the Blues and her 100th overall game in the Women’s Super League was midfielder Walsh. The England international marked the occasion with a stunning strike from outside the box and an assist for James in our third goal of the afternoon, and Bompastor discussed how the Chelsea coaching staff have been encouraging Walsh to shoot. ‘I'm really happy with Keira,’ continued the head coach. ‘She's one of these players and leaders in my team who really sets the tone for the way we want to play. She controls and manages the game in a perfect way in terms of how I want the team to play. In possession of the ball, she's really good. We are really encouraging her to take opportunities from the edge of the box. ‘She has a great shot, and she still has more to come. It’s a case of her being confident, and today she was unbelievable. Many other players were also unbelievable. I think even out of possession today we were a good team. The counter-press was good, the intensity was high, and even when we lost the ball, we reacted quickly. We always put the United players under pressure everywhere on the pitch. ‘There are some good learnings for us to take for our confidence, but we're still early in the season, and now it's up to us to be able to sustain those types of performances.’

news.title: Kaptein's post-United thoughts
Sonia reflects on Man Utd win
Keira Walsh on 'amazing feeling' of reaching 50 appearances for Chelsea
news.body_en: Keira Walsh marked her 50th appearance for the Blues with a stunning strike from outside the box and an assist in our 5-0 victory against Manchester United. It was a happy day for the Blues midfielder as she netted one of her trademark goals from range on her 50th outing for Chelsea and also passed the 100-appearance marker in the Women's Super League. The England international moved to Chelsea from Barcelona at the end of January 2025 and made her Blues debut two days later in a 1-0 win away at Aston Villa. Walsh soon became a regular in our starting XI and helped us to a domestic Treble at the end of her first campaign in Blue. The midfield playmaker has now scored four goals for the Blues during her half-century of appearances 'Playing that many games for such a good club is obviously an amazing feeling,' said Walsh upon reaching the milestone. 'Winning the league was a highlight for me because it's not an easy league to win, and that's what I came here to do. 'The Chelsea fans have really welcomed me from when I first came and always supported the way that I've played. I want to keep playing good football, enjoying it, and hopefully reach 100 in blue.' In addition to her 50 Chelsea appearances, Walsh has amassed 103 senior England caps, winning the Women's European Championship in 2022 and 2025 and reaching the Women's World Cup final in 2023.

news.title: Match Report: Manchester United 0-5 Chelsea
news.body_en: Keira Walsh scored and assisted on her 50th Blues appearance as Chelsea delivered a 5-0 away win at Manchester United in the Women's Super League. We faced a new-look Manchester United side who were led by new boss Eva Olid after they had parted ways with their head coach Marc Skinner in the summer, following his five-year spell in charge of the club. After an initial exchange of chances, Chelsea began to assert our dominance in the game. It was Sjoeke Nusken – playing in a more advanced role than normal – who opened the scoring with a composed finish from a Wieke Kaptein assist. Doubling our advantage on the half-hour mark was Keira Walsh, who let fly with a powerful drive into the bottom corner to take a firm grip of the contest. The home side worked hard but were no match for the Blues, and Lauren James put us three goals to the good with a clinical finish after an hour. Ellie Carpenter then ended all hope of a comeback for the Red Devils when she kept her head to finish her own rebound, putting us 4-0 up. We added our fifth and final goal from a corner routine. Bronze reacted first to pick up the ball in the box, and the left-back smashed home from close range to complete the rout. The team answered Bompastor's call for them to be more clinical after last week's draw with Aston Villa, Walsh grabbed a goal and an assist on her 50th Chelsea appearance, and there were also Women's Super League debuts for substitutes Giulia Dragoni and Nelly Las in a day that was packed with positives. Bompastor made two changes to her starting XI ahead of this clash, switching Veerle Buurman for Kadeisha Buchanan and bringing in Chelsea Academy graduate Lexi Potter in place of striker Aggie Beever-Jones. Alongside Potter in the midfield was the experienced Walsh, who passed the 50-appearance marker for Chelsea with her place in the starting line-up. On the bench was defender Nathalie Bjorn, having made her recovery from a lengthy injury layoff. When the match kicked off, it was clear that the versatile Nusken had been deployed in an advanced attacking role, with James in the central striker position. Both sides traded chances in the early stages of the encounter, as Elisabeth Terland tested the gloves of Hannah Hampton, while Katie McCabe made life difficult for Phallon Tullis-Joyce with a cross-cum-shot which dipped dramatically and went just over the bar. With 15 minutes gone, Potter played a neat sideways pass into James on the left-hand side, for the No.10 to swing in a cross to the far post to pick out Wieke Kaptein. The Netherlands international's headed effort was collected gratefully by Tullis Joyce, but there were signs the Blues were finding the spaces in attack. We breached the home side's defences after a prolonged spell of pressure and neat play around the penalty area with 20 minutes gone. Kaptein capitalised on a moment of hesitation in the opposition backline and fed the ball to Nusken, and the Germany international slotted home with a composed finish. Our defence had to switch on to protect our advantage minutes later, when Buchanan made a perfectly timed sliding block inside the penalty area to put the ball out for a corner. The Blues continued to dominate possession and drove forward with every given opportunity. And when Bronze played the ball to international team-mate Walsh on the edge of the box, the midfielder seized her chance to drill the ball towards goal. The shot was as clean as they come, and it flew into the bottom corner to mark Walsh's 50th Chelsea appearance in style. With the half-time whistle approaching, James saw her curling effort palmed away by Tullis-Joyce, before Carpenter had a close-range shot well blocked on the follow-up. The Blues were hungry for more after the break. James struck the ball into the danger area, but Alyssa Thompson couldn't quite get there for what would've been an easy tap-in as it trickled along the goal-line. The American then switched roles with the No.10 as she got round her marker on the left and put a cross in, but Thompson couldn't direct her shot goalwards. Yet it wasn't long before James had her second in as many WSL matches. Played in with a killer pass from Walsh, the forward slotted home with confidence, getting her just reward for an excellent display. With the home side disheartened, Chelsea pushed on. Carpenter found herself in a position to shoot and initially stung the gloves of Tullis-Joyce, but when the rebound fell nicely at her feet, she had the opportunity to have another go and this time side-footed her shot into the back of the net. Substitute Sandy Baltimore also went close later on, and Buchanan slid in with another incredible block at the other end as the match ended with Man United limited to just two shots on goal by the Blues backline. Deep into stoppage time, Bronze scored her first of the campaign with an emphatic finish from close-range. This was a truly dominant display from Chelsea, one that will give Bompastor and her team confidence as we move forward in the new campaign. We take our points tally to four after our first two WSL matches of the season. We return to Stamford Bridge in WSL action when we face Birmingham City next Saturday lunchtime, with kick-off set for 12.45pm. news.title: Chavarria on working hard to solve problems
news.body_en: Pep Chavarria felt it was another strong attacking display from Chelsea against Hull City, but we need to work hard on the training pitch to sure up our defence in future. Despite taking an early lead through Morgan Rogers on Saturday, two goals in six minutes left the Blues chasing the game in the second half. We got back on level terms thanks to Joao Pedro’s third Premier League goal of the season, but had to settle for a 2-2 draw at the final whistle. It’s important to remember the context, as the Tigers remain unbeaten in the league and were yet to concede a goal this season until their visit to Stamford Bridge. However, for Chavarria, the lesson to take from this match was clear. ‘It was a difficult game. Of course, Hull is a very good team,’ said our Spanish full-back. ‘I think that when we scored the first goal we controlled the game, but when they equalised Hull did good things. Our team is very competitive and we always have a lot of energy to score goals, but we need to defend better, I think that is the key. ‘Hull want to play long balls and box-to-box. It's difficult because you stay in their area and then you need to defend in our area. They like to run and you need to defend those actions. ‘I think that the team did a good game, but we conceded two goals, so we need to work hard and we need to solve the problems.’ Chavarria came off the bench at half-time to make his fourth Premier League appearance since joining the Blues from Rayo Vallecano this summer. Although it wasn’t enough to take all three points, the 28-year-old felt the way we came out swinging for the second half demonstrated why he is so pleased to be at Chelsea, where he is settling in well. ‘I think that in the second half we had more energy, more intensity, to win the duels,’ he continued. ‘This team has a lot of talent and it's a pleasure to play with these top players, because we have a lot of alternatives and solutions. ‘For me it's a dream to be here and I'm very happy. I feel very good now and I think that the adaptation is good.’

news.title: Alonso outlines how time will help Blues learn and improve
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has reiterated that his Chelsea side must continue to ‘learn from everything’ after our draw with Hull City, but has emphasised that the Blues will only continue to improve in time. Our latest Premier League outing ended in what the Spaniard admitted was a disappointing result. We had taken the lead against the Tigers at Stamford Bridge yesterday, with Morgan Rogers firing us into a seventh-minute lead. However, two goals in the space of six first-half minutes from Mohamed Belloumi put Hull ahead at the interval. The Blues then had to battle back into the contest. We managed to pull level through a fine Joao Pedro finish and pushed hard for a winner. Yet Hull, who hadn’t conceded a goal in the top flight before their trip to west London, were resolute to earn a share of the points. The draw means the Blues have taken seven points from our opening four Premier League games. It’s a solid start, although one Alonso knows could have been better. However, with less than a month of competitive football played, the Spaniard appreciates it’s natural there is still plenty of room for improvement during the season. He said: ‘It’s early days for us. It’s one month together and in one month, we know the idea, the concepts, the mentality, but it’s too early to know it’s already built. ‘It will take longer, but we need to learn from everything and from this [against Hull] as well. ‘For sure, I think it will come. At the moment, we are not having that feeling we are solid enough. With work and with games, I think it will get better.’ On the defensive frailty of his side, which has seen the Blues concede at least twice in all of our Premier League matches this term, Alonso added: ‘Overall, I think we are attacking better than we are defending. In every aspect, so we know that it’s a big topic and a theme for us. ‘For sure, it’s just four games, but the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness and competitive sense, we can do better.’

news.title: Joao Pedro: We need to improve on the details
news.body_en: Joao Pedro believes Chelsea made a strong start against Hull City, but need to improve quickly to avoid dropping more points after having to settle for just one in Saturday’s Premier League meeting with the Tigers. Not for the first time this season, the Blues began the match on the front foot and, as the game approached the half-hour mark, there was little sign of what was to come. Morgan Rogers fired us into a seventh-minute lead after being found on the edge of the box by Joao Pedro, but two quick-fire Hull goals left us trailing, until the Brazilian smashed an equaliser into the roof of the net. We couldn’t find a third goal to take all three points, the game ending in a 2-2 draw, leaving the Blues determined to keep improving to do better next time out. ‘I think we started really well,’ reflected Joao Pedro. ‘We put pressure on them, we controlled the game, but we need to improve on the details because I think in the end, this point is very important for us. So we need to analyse and improve. ‘We have to adapt quickly, as soon as possible, because we know how the Premier League is. If you drop points, in the end it will be difficult to recover. We need to adapt quickly because if you want to compete, you have to improve on that. ‘We knew if they got in front they were going to sit at the back and wait for us to come and play for the counter-attack. It was a tough game. ‘In the end, we could get one point, but like I said, we need to improve and I think we're going to improve soon.’ It was another fine individual performance from Joao Pedro, the August Premier League Player of the Month taking his tally to three goals and three assists in four games in that competition this season. Again, he was helped by the instant connection he has developed with fellow forwards Palmer and Rogers, as shown when the former provided the low cross for the equaliser. ‘When Cole passed to me I just tried to hit it on target and I was very happy to hit a good shot,’ the striker continued. ‘I enjoy [playing with Palmer and Rogers] a lot because they are very good players and I know when we play close, we can be very dangerous. We showed that again. So I enjoy it a lot and hopefully we can continue to improve even more.’ Joao Pedro also responded to the comparison made by Xabi Alonso on Friday between our Brazilian and the France and Real Madrid legend Karim Benzema. ‘I think maybe the style, the way I play – I like to come deep and I like to link up with my team-mates,’ he added. ‘But, of course, Benzema is on another level. ‘I just try to enjoy every game and try to help my team with goals or assists. I'm in a very good moment and I'm very happy.’

news.title: Full Match: Chelsea vs Hull City
Extended: Chelsea 2-2 Hull City
Match gallery: Blues left frustrated by Tigers
Match report: Chelsea 2-2 Hull City
news.body_en: Supporters at Stamford Bridge have certainly not been starved of entertainment this season. Unfortunately, the Blues' latest back-and-forth game ended with Hull City leaving west London with a 2-2 draw and a point. Xabi Alonso's side had, once again, made an impressive start. We were ahead inside seven minutes against the Tigers, as Morgan Rogers collected a Joao Pedro pass and slammed home a finish at the near post. The Blues appeared in control of the game, but two quick-fire Hull goals from Mohamed Belloumi meant we trailed at the break. Another comeback was required if we were to win. We got halfway there. In the 66th minute, Joao Pedro drove a left-footed strike into the net after a cross from Cole Palmer. Further chances came and went in the time that remained. Yet on this occasion, we couldn't find a winner as Hull held on for a share of the spoils. Alonso made two changes to the side that started our last Premier League outing at Arsenal. Josh Acheampong and Maxence Lacroix stepped out of the back line, with Malo Gusto and Levi Colwill coming in. The Blues set up with a back four ahead of Emi Martinez. Wesley Fofana and Jorrel Hato were included in defence alongside Gusto and Colwill, Reece James partnered Romeo Lavia in midfield, while Pedro Neto, Cole Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro were in our attack. Hull arrived at Stamford Bridge having not conceded in their opening three games. Alonso's side, meanwhile, have developed a habit of scoring early this term – and we did so once more. Just seven minutes had elapsed when Palmer collected possession in the Hull half and fed a pass into the feet of Joao Pedro. The Brazilian turned and moved the ball to Rogers, who shifted it onto his left foot and drove a near-post shot beyond Konstantinos Tzolakis. Going behind didn't alter Hull's approach. The Tigers sat deep and attempted to soak up pressure. It left few gaps for the Blues to exploit, but a chance was fashioned for Neto after the ball was won back in midfield. It enabled the Blues to counter and after Joao Pedro found the Portuguese winger breaking into the penalty area, Neto tried to guide a shot into the far corner. Tzolakis was alert, though, and pushed the attempt wide. From set-pieces, we carried a threat. One low James cross into the near-post was guided narrowly wide by Neto, while our skipper came close with a whipped delivery that Tzolakis saved. As the goalkeeper looked to restart play, he collided with Colwill and needed treatment. It proved a turning point in the half. After the stoppage, Tzolakis restarted the game. He punted the ball long and Hull wing-back Ryan Giles chased it to the byline and hooked it into the Chelsea penalty area. Hato misjudged the flight, and then the bounce, and Belloumi was able to power a measured strike beyond Martinez. The unexpected goal swung momentum in Hull's favour and the visitors took full advantage by grabbing a quick-fire second. Colwill had done excellently to deflect a goal-bound shot from Lewie Coyle behind, but from the resulting corner a Semi Ajayi header struck the crossbar. The rebound fell to McBurnie and he teed up Belloumi, whose shot was deflected on its way into the net. Hull's six-minute gut-punch blunted the Blues for the remainder of the half. A Gusto shot deflected wide and a late corner cleared behind from under his crossbar by a Hull defender was the best we offered. At the interval, Alonso introduced Pep Chavarria for Hato. The shape stayed the same, but there was greater urgency to our possession. Rogers' physicality when running with the ball was causing problems for the Hull back line, and he was fouled twice in quick succession. James took both free-kicks. The Chelsea captain tried to catch out Tzolakis at his near-post first, before he whipped another attempt from 25 yards over the wall and toward the top corner. The Hull goalkeeper clawed it away. After a break in play following a collision of heads involving Joao Pedro and Nobel Mendy, the Tigers fashioned a chance. Regan Slater was given time to line up a shot and he powered the ball at Martinez, who beat the effort away and then reacted well to stop the ball from reaching Oli McBurnie. Hull's backline was proving difficult to break down. But with 24 minutes to play, we found a way through. Palmer claimed the assist, as he drove to the byline down the Blues' left and crossed low for Joao Pedro. The ball was slightly behind the Brazilian, yet he readjusted expertly and drilled a left-footed finish into the roof of the net. The Blues were level and there was plenty of time to fashion a winner. Given Hull's resilience, that wouldn't be easy, and Alonso introduced Valentin Barco and Danny Welbeck for Lavia and Gusto to try to help us find a way through. Hull's threat diminished as the game moved closer to a conclusion. We had chances, with James having a low shot saved and Palmer guiding an attempt over from inside the penalty area. The best opportunity for a Blues winner fell to Rogers. After a Hull break was snuffed out by Colwill, he broke forward, found Welbeck, who passed to Palmer. The England international evaluated his options and spotted Rogers racing forward. Palmer's pass was on point and Rogers controlled and fired at goal. Unfortunately, it was too close to Tzolakis, who saved. Hull, meanwhile, almost snatched all three points in the final minutes, as a ball across the box was met by Mohamed-Ali Cho. His attempt was on target but Martinez was down to save. Six minutes were added. Estevao, introduced late on, worked Tzolakis at his near post. The Brazilian then forced a late penalty appeal for handball against Ajayi. Nothing was given. There was one last opportunity. After a break led by Estevao was halted on the edge of the Hull box, we were awarded a free-kick 20 yards from goal. Palmer lined it up. It would be the final chance of the game. Unfortunately, Palmer's effort was too high and the referee followed it with the full-time whistle. The points were shared. The Blues sit fourth in the Premier League table, with seven points secured from our opening four matches. Alonso's side have a free week before we make the short journey to the Gtech Community Stadium to face Brentford on Friday evening. Kick-off at our west London neighbours is at 8pm. news.title: Alonso on Hull draw: 'We got what we deserved'
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso says his Chelsea side are taking steps forward, but acknowledges there are 'some parts of the game that are compulsory to improve to compete better in the Premier League' following today's 2-2 draw with Hull City. Our latest outing at Stamford Bridge was another entertaining, back-and-forth contest, with the Blues once again making a fast start as Morgan Rogers fired us ahead after seven minutes. We appeared to have the game under control, only for two quick-fire goals from Mohamed Belloumi to send us into the half-time interval behind. In the second period, Joao Pedro levelled with a fine finish and we pushed hard for a winner. Unfortunately, it didn't arrive. Alonso was disappointed with the nature of the goals conceded by the Blues, admitting after the full-time whistle that our progress is being hindered by a defensive fragility. He said: 'We are taking steps forward, but we would like to have the feeling we are further. We know we will get there, but at the moment, there are some parts of the game that are compulsory to improve to compete better in the Premier League. 'We need to be more solid and be competing for the whole game, not just for some parts of the game. That consistency in performance is something that we need. That is clear and we know it’s a process, but that is where we will make the biggest improvement. 'We are confident in that [attacking] part, but we need to have the balance to be confident in the other part to be closer to winning games. Today we were not far but we got what we deserved today.' Alonso's side have had little issue in the attacking third, with the Blues scoring 18 goals in our six matches thus far in all competitions. Yet the Blues manager has stressed the need for greater balance to ensure our goal-scoring prowess is always rewarded with victories. ‘It may be entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game – that we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,' he explained. 'Especially on the first goal, we can do much better; it was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling the game and creating chances. 'The momentum we had changed a little bit [after their equaliser], and the mood and the score of the game. It’s something we need to talk about and address. We will get better, but it is having an impact on our performances.'

PL2 report: Arsenal U21s 1-4 Cobham Next Gen
news.body_en: Chelsea Cobham Next Gen produced a memorable performance to defeat London rivals Arsenal 4-1 in Premier League 2. Leo Black opened the scoring after 14 minutes, before Reggie Watson made it three penalties in three PL2 games this season shortly before the interval. The midfielder added his second with a superb free-kick after the break to put Harry Hudson’s side three goals ahead. James Scanlon reduced the deficit for Arsenal, but Chizaram Ezenwata rounded off the scoring in stoppage time following a through-ball from Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli. Harrison Bettoni had our first sight of goal after six minutes, seeing his left-footed effort from distance blocked. Chelsea went ahead eight minutes later. Sol Gordon’s right-footed shot was blocked, but the ball fell straight to Black, who finished neatly into the bottom corner. Ezenwata dragged an effort just wide of the left post before the Blues threatened twice in quick succession. Nicoll-Jazuli worked space inside the box but was denied by Jack Porter, who then pushed away Gordon’s effort towards the bottom corner. Nicoll-Jazuli won a penalty in the 40th minute when he was fouled. Watson stepped up and struck low into the bottom-left corner to double our advantage before the break. Nicoll-Jazuli tested Porter from outside the box shortly after the restart, then fired just over from a central position a minute later. Harrison McMahon had a long-range strike blocked before Watson extended Chelsea’s lead in the 72nd minute, with his excellent free-kick clipping the post on its way in. Kendry Paez replaced Bettoni before Ezenwata sent another effort narrowly wide. Arsenal pulled a goal back in the 79th minute through Scanlon, who finished into the bottom-left corner. Lewi Richards came on for Alfie Osborne and Calvin Diakite replaced Gordon as the Blues made further changes. Ezenwata then added our fourth five minutes into stoppage time. Nicoll-Jazuli showed great feet before threading the ball through for the striker to finish into the bottom-left corner expertly. Cobham Next Gen have now won two of their three PL2 matches this season. Our opening day loss to Bournemouth means we are in seventh place but just one point below leaders Fulham. news.title: Pep reacts to home draw
Under-18 Premier League report: Brighton & Hove Albion 1-5 Chelsea
news.body_en: Jashayde Greenwood bagged a hat-trick as he helped Chelsea Under-18s come from behind to beat Brighton & Hove Albion 5-1 in the Under-18 Premier League. Mason Stephens gave the hosts an early lead, but Greenwood brought the Blues level on the half-hour. Andrew Pennie put Dan Hogan’s side ahead shortly after the interval before Greenwood added a penalty and completed his treble late on. Heze Grimwade rounded off the scoring in the final minute of normal time, finishing from goalkeeper Toby Bell’s long ball forward. Brighton went ahead after eight minutes, Stephens beating Bell with a low finish after being through one-on-one. Chelsea’s first effort came through Jacob Hall, whose left-footed shot from outside the area was saved. Pennie then fired wide and had another attempt blocked before Greenwood struck just over. The equaliser arrived in the 30th minute. Charlie Wilson-Papps could not hold Grimwade’s low cross after a slick passing move and Greenwood followed up to finish from close range. Grimwade had a shot from distance charged down before the break, with the sides going in level. Grimwade tested Wilson-Papps with a free-kick two minutes after the restart and was denied again shortly afterwards, his right-footed effort saved low. The Blues moved ahead in the 53rd minute when Brighton failed to clear their lines and Pennie was there to apply the finish. Wilson-Papps continued to keep Chelsea out, pushing away Eden Mahoney-Smith’s low strike before saving Grimwade’s effort from a tight angle at the foot of the post. Our third came with 20 minutes remaining. Fraser Widdop brought down Grimwade inside the area and Greenwood converted the penalty into the bottom corner. Isago Silva replaced Hall in the 74th minute, with Trey Faromo-Adebayo coming on for Pennie a minute later. Greenwood completed his hat-trick three minutes from time, his cross-shot taking a deflection off Frankie Pope and looping into the far corner. Wilson-Papps denied him a fourth at the near post, but Chelsea added another in the 90th minute. Bell’s long kick sent Grimwade through and he rounded the goalkeeper to finish right-footed into the bottom corner. The Blues are fourth in the Under-18 Premier League South table after three wins from our five games so far, meaning we are four points below leaders Tottenham Hotspur. news.title: Alonso details what's needed to overcome Hull City
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes a performance that includes ‘good tempo and concentration’ will give his Chelsea side the best chance of defeating Hull City at Stamford Bridge. The newly-promoted Tigers have made an impressive start to the campaign. They have taken seven points from their opening three fixtures and are yet to concede a goal. We enter today’s contest following a come-from-behind victory over Leeds United in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. Alonso has made nine changes to the side that started in midweek, with only Levi Colwill and Malo Gusto keeping their places. That means our starting XI consists of Emi Martinez, Wesley Fofana, Colwill, Jorrel Hato, Malo Gusto, captain Reece James, Romeo Lavia, Gusto, Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro. It’s a side full of quality, but Alonso knows the Blues will need to produce another high-tempo performance to claim all three points. ‘We come from an intense game against Leeds on Wednesday, but all of them are fine and it’s a good team for today,’ Alonso said ahead of the game. ‘We are hoping for a win; let’s see how we make it. For sure it’s going to be tough and Hull City have started really well. But if we are on top of our game and play with good tempo and concentration, we will have a good chance.’ We have yet to keep a clean sheet this term, something Alonso discussed in the build-up to the game. Yet the Spaniard is not fixated on a shutout, with his primary focus on claiming victory. ‘First the win, and then if we can win with a clean sheet then that’s better,’ he said.

news.title: Confirmed Chelsea line up vs Hull City
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has made nine changes to his Chelsea side for this afternoon's Premier League clash with Hull City. After a barnstorming midweek Carabao Cup tie, when the Blues came from two goals down to record a 6-3 win over Leeds United, it's back to top-flight action this afternoon at Stamford Bridge. It's Hull's first Premier League visit since January 2017, and the newly-promoted Tigers arrive having taken seven points from their opening three fixtures without conceding a goal. While several changes were made to Wednesday night's starting XI, there are just two alterations to the side that began our last league outing against Arsenal in today's team sheet. Emi Martinez returns in goal for the Blues and is expected to be protected by a back three consisting of Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill and Jorrel Hato. Malo Gusto and Pedro Neto are set to occupy the wing-back roles, with Reece James and Romeo Lavia in central midfield. The front three of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro are reinstated into the starting XI, with Danny Welbeck among the Blues substitutes. Chelsea: Martinez, Fofana, Colwill, Hato, Gusto, James (c), Lavia, Neto, Palmer, Rogers, Joao Pedro Substitutes: Penders, Acheampong, Lacroix, Chavarria, Barco, Quenda, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck

Alonso: Emotional control and patience key to breaking down low blocks
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has detailed the tactical mindset required when facing teams set up in a low defensive block, with our manager emphasising the importance of patience, control and calmness. The Blues have scored early in each of our three league games so far this season, something Alonso knows cannot last forever. And should we not net early against Hull City today, we will likely face the challenge of breaking down a low block. The Tigers have impressed with three consecutive shutouts so far this season – just the third promoted side to achieve that in Premier League history – and Alonso appreciates the challenge that facing a deep-lying defence can present. ‘You need to do many things right,’ Alonso said. ‘You need to be patient. You need to be patient in positioning, patient in dynamics, patient in knowing when to attack and when it is the right moment. ‘There will be different moments as well. It’s not that I expect it’s going to be 90 minutes only one way. You need to be prepared for different contexts and scenarios, but the key is not to get frustrated, knowing that the details are so important. ‘We played against Luton when they were in a low block, and at half-time it was 0-0,' added Alonso. 'But half-time was really relaxed. We said, "We are doing it right, keep going, keep going, keep going." Once we scored the first goal, it changed. But we need to be ready for everything.’ Alonso’s venerable Premier League career taught him plenty about the standards required in the top flight, but also the fine margins that can make the difference in tight contests. Balancing those with the bigger picture is something he wants to instil in his Chelsea squad. ‘Set-pieces can play an important part,’ Alonso said. ‘But I always think that if you have game control, you get emotional control. 'Not losing emotional control of the game is always good, and having the conviction that what you’re doing is the best way to beat Hull, or any team operating in a low block.’

Joao Pedro: 'A special moment for me' 💙
Alonso on Joao Pedro: ‘He reminds me of Benzema’
news.body_en: There can be no arguing who the Premier League’s outstanding performer was in August. Joao Pedro deservedly received the league’s monthly prize and Xabi Alonso has added his name to the list of people praising our Brazilian striker. Joao Pedro scored and assisted in the wins over Fulham and Brighton and Hove Albion that got our 2026/27 campaign off to the perfect start. He duly received the Premier League Player of the Month award for the first time in a career that is continuing to reach new heights. Alonso has only spent a couple of months working with Joao Pedro, but it is already clear to our manager what an outstanding talent he has at his disposal. ‘He's been top, not just football-wise but personality-wise, his maturity,’ said Alonso. ‘He has a very strong goal this year: to have a great season, to score many goals, to be a [Player of the Month] nominee not just this month, but for more months. ‘I'm really not surprised, but am really happy with the kind of player that we have with Joao.’ Alonso has no qualms putting Joao Pedro in the same category as Erling Haaland when it comes to the Premier League’s top strikers. And it is not only Joao Pedro’s goal contributions that have impressed Alonso; his all-round centre-forward play has contributed to the dynamic attacking performances the Blues have produced thus far under the Blues manager. In fact, our No.9’s strengths bring to mind one of Alonso’s former Real Madrid team-mates – and one of the greatest of all time. ‘As a profile of striker, he seems to be able to do everything,’ said Alonso. ‘He reminds me of (Karim) Benzema because he's good in the box, he's good out of the box, he's good coming to the left side, good with the head. He's very complete. He's intelligent. ‘So yes, he’s still young, and he still has things to develop, but he has many absolutely outstanding qualities.’ We look forward to seeing them on show again today when Hull City visit the Bridge.

news.title: Chavarria shares his journey from lower league to Chelsea
news.body_en: Pep Chavarria discusses his extraordinary rise from the Spanish lower leagues to Chelsea in an exclusive interview with the matchday programme for this Saturday’s Premier League game against Hull City. The Catalan full-back was born in the hometown of Salvador Dali, and it has been a surreal journey to the top of the game for him, beginning as a 16-year-old with local club Unio Esportiva Figueres, in the fourth tier, and then stepping up division by division to the highest echelons of European football in the 12 years that have followed. 'I learned a lot about footballers in those days,' he says of those early seasons in the game. 'Some players would train in the morning with the football club and in the afternoon they would work in another job. 'I think all my career, I always had a lot of patience, plus hard work and commitment. And I have always been positive because, well, football players, we always want everything very quickly. Everything. But sometimes you need to be patient and just stay focused on the everyday, on improving. And I think this is the key.' The 28-year-old – who signed from Rayo Vallecano in the summer – has gleaned plenty of wisdom en route to Stamford Bridge and he meets every challenge head on. 'I didn’t start in a big academy and I had to work hard,' he adds. 'I don’t know why, but I was always thinking that I wanted to become a professional football player. I wanted it, I really wanted it. I think that everything is possible if you work hard and you have a good mentality, and a good circle of friends and family.' The programme team have also been in nostalgic mood this week. The latest instalment of our Greatest Games series reflects on our 4-0 win over Hull in May 1977, when Chelsea fans celebrated promotion back to the top flight with Eddie McCreadie and his team of young Blues. Then there is a special Legacy feature marking 60 years of the Shed at Stamford Bridge with tales from the terraces by supporters who made it their home over the course of the decades. There is all the latest news from around the club, plus everything you need to know going into the game. So make sure you pick up a copy from the programme sellers around the stadium, or order online from our official publications partner, Reach Sport.

news.title: Chelsea vs Hull City: All you need to know
news.body_en: Chelsea host Hull City at Stamford Bridge sat fourth in the Premier League table. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton look ahead to our first traditional 3pm Saturday kick-off of the season. This fixture comes 121 years and one day after Hull became the Blues’ first competitive opponents at Stamford Bridge on 11 September 1905. The visitors have been the surprise package of the current season, placed third and yet to concede a goal, three fixtures into their return to the top flight. Only two promoted clubs had previously achieved that feat – Charlton Athletic in 1998 and Huddersfield Town in 2017. Xabi Alonso will be determined to rewrite Chelsea’s recent history at home to Premier League new boys, after no win in four matches since consecutive victories against Southampton and Leicester City in 2025. On Tuesday at Sunderland, the Tigers lost 1-0 in the Carabao Cup (their first defeat of the season), though Sergej Jakirovic made eight changes to their line-up from the previous weekend. A day later in the same competition, Chelsea even outshone the floodlights at the Bridge, storming back from 2-0 down to beat ancient rivals Leeds United 6-3, with substitute Morgan Rogers contributing three assists. The last time this fixture was on the Premier League schedule in 2016/17, Antonio Conte’s Blues won 2-0 home and away, with Diego Costa scoring in both games. Chelsea’s run of hosting Hull 18 times in the league without loss is the Blues’ best record against any club and City’s worst. Chelsea and Hull have met 49 times across all competitions, but only 10 times in the top flight. The Humberside club have scored just three league goals over their 18 visits to the Fulham Road. The Tigers were the first side ever to visit Stamford Bridge for a Division Two fixture on 11 September 1905, Jimmy Windridge (three goals) and David Copeland (two goals) starring in a 5-1 thrashing. Their most celebrated visit was the final match of the Division Two season on 14 May 1977, a 4-0 win for Chelsea that became a promotion party. Twice play was stopped by boisterous fans encroaching onto the pitch as Ian Britton netted one and Steve Finnieston grabbed a hat-trick. Inspirational manager Eddie McCreadie even pleaded with fans over the public address system to stay calm and remain on the terraces. Hull have never beaten the Blues in London and their last victory at home was 18 meetings back. Chelsea have won 15 of the 17 matches on all fronts since (including each of the last nine) and drawn two. Chelsea are three goals short of 100 against Hull across all competitions. Only Portsmouth (14) have played more Premier League matches against the Blues without victory than Hull (10). The three most recent encounters between the two teams were all FA Cup wins for the Blues, in 2018, 2020 and February this year, with an aggregate score of 10-1. Chelsea have become the first team ever to score within five minutes of the start in each of their opening three Premier League fixtures. Joao Pedro was fouled six times by Arsenal, the most suffered by a single player in any Premier League match this season. On Wednesday, in the 6-3 Carabao Cup defeat of Leeds, the Blues netted six second-half goals for the first time since the 8-0 win over Wigan Athletic in May 2010, which clinched the Premier League title. Our 16-year-old midweek debutant Reggie Watson was 14 weeks old back then and his father Ben started for the Latics. Our record victory in the League Cup, 7-0 at Doncaster Rovers in 1960, also featured a six-goal second-half salvo.

news.title: Hull game travel warning - Fulham Broadway closed; District Line disruption
news.body_en: Supporters intending to travel to or from Saturday’s home Premier League game against Hull City using the London Underground are advised that planned engineering works may affect your journey. The District Line is closed west of Tower Hill Station and on the whole of the Edgware Road branch, including the line down to Wimbledon. This means for the match at Stamford Bridge, Fulham Broadway Station is closed all day and there are no District Line trains running to any nearby stations on that branch of the tube network. The Circle Line is also affected and is closed between Edgware Road and Aldgate (via Victoria).
